objectives.objective_text: Define a cell and explain why cells are considered the basic unit of life.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a cell?
questions.choice_a: The basic unit of life that carries out life functions
questions.choice_b: A type of tissue found only in animals
questions.choice_c: A small organ inside the body
questions.choice_d: A nonliving particle too small to affect organisms

questions.stem: Which evidence best supports the claim that living things are made of cells?
questions.choice_a: Living things move from place to place
questions.choice_b: Under a microscope, living things show one or more cells
questions.choice_c: Living things have different colors
questions.choice_d: Living things are found in many environments

questions.stem: A student says, "If it is alive, you can see it moving." Which choice best corrects this idea?
questions.choice_a: All living things move fast enough to see
questions.choice_b: Some living things are too small to see without tools, and many do not move in ways you can see
questions.choice_c: Only animals are living things
questions.choice_d: If something does not move, it cannot grow

questions.stem: Which item is alive based on the idea that living things are made of cells?
questions.choice_a: A crystal of salt
questions.choice_b: A plastic bead
questions.choice_c: A bacterium
questions.choice_d: A raindrop

questions.stem: Which statement is the best claim about living things and cells?
questions.choice_a: Only animals are made of cells
questions.choice_b: Living things are made of cells, either one cell or many cells
questions.choice_c: Cells are made of organs
questions.choice_d: All cells look exactly the same

questions.stem: A student observes many tiny boxes in a thin slice of onion under a microscope. What is the best explanation?
questions.choice_a: The boxes are cells that make up the onion tissue
questions.choice_b: The boxes are air bubbles that prove the onion is nonliving
questions.choice_c: The boxes are organs inside the onion
questions.choice_d: The boxes are pieces of dirt stuck to the onion

questions.stem: Why is a microscope useful when studying whether something is made of cells?
questions.choice_a: It makes cells larger so they can be seen
questions.choice_b: It changes cells into organs
questions.choice_c: It proves that all cells are the same size
questions.choice_d: It removes cells so only tissues remain

objectives.objective_text: Distinguish between unicellular and multicellular organisms using evidence and examples.

questions.stem: What is a unicellular organism?
questions.choice_a: An organism made of one cell that carries out all life functions
questions.choice_b: An organism made of many different types of cells
questions.choice_c: A single organ inside a larger organism
questions.choice_d: A group of tissues working together

questions.stem: Which organism is most likely unicellular?
questions.choice_a: A mushroom
questions.choice_b: A bacterium
questions.choice_c: A tree
questions.choice_d: A fish

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a multicellular organism?
questions.choice_a: It is made of one cell that does everything
questions.choice_b: It is made of many cells, often with different types of cells doing different jobs
questions.choice_c: It has no cells because it is too large
questions.choice_d: It is alive only when it moves

questions.stem: A student claims, "An organism with only one cell cannot be alive." Which choice is the best rebuttal?
questions.choice_a: One cell can still take in materials, use energy, and reproduce
questions.choice_b: Only multicellular organisms can use energy
questions.choice_c: Unicellular organisms are made of nonliving parts only
questions.choice_d: Unicellular organisms are too small to be considered alive

questions.stem: A microscope view shows a sample with thousands of similar-looking cells connected together. What is the best conclusion?
questions.choice_a: The sample is from a unicellular organism
questions.choice_b: The sample is from a multicellular organism
questions.choice_c: The sample is nonliving because there are too many cells
questions.choice_d: The sample is an organ, not an organism

questions.stem: Which evidence best supports that a plant is multicellular?
questions.choice_a: A plant stays in one place
questions.choice_b: A plant has many cells visible in different tissues under a microscope
questions.choice_c: A plant is green
questions.choice_d: A plant grows toward light

questions.stem: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.choice_a: Unicellular: human; Multicellular: amoeba
questions.choice_b: Unicellular: bacterium; Multicellular: dog
questions.choice_c: Unicellular: tree; Multicellular: yeast
questions.choice_d: Unicellular: fish; Multicellular: virus

objectives.objective_text: Use investigation evidence to argue whether a sample is living based on the presence of one or more cells.

questions.stem: Students investigate two water samples under a microscope. Sample A shows moving single-celled organisms. Sample B shows no cells. Which claim is best supported?
questions.choice_a: Both samples are living because they contain water
questions.choice_b: Sample A is living because it contains cells; Sample B may be nonliving because no cells were found
questions.choice_c: Sample B is living because it has no cells
questions.choice_d: Neither sample is living because cells must be seen without tools

questions.stem: A student finds tiny structures in a sample, but they are not organized like cells and do not repeat in a pattern. What is the best next step in the investigation?
questions.choice_a: Conclude the sample is living without more evidence
questions.choice_b: Adjust the microscope focus and examine multiple areas to look for cells
questions.choice_c: Stop using the microscope because it cannot show cells
questions.choice_d: Assume the sample is multicellular

questions.stem: Which statement is the best reasoning to connect evidence to the claim "The sample is living"?
questions.choice_a: It looks interesting under the microscope
questions.choice_b: Living things are made of cells, and cells were observed in the sample
questions.choice_c: It was collected outside
questions.choice_d: It moved when the slide was tapped

questions.stem: A student says a paper clip is alive because it moves when a magnet is near. Which evidence best refutes the claim?
questions.choice_a: A paper clip is shiny
questions.choice_b: A paper clip is cold to the touch
questions.choice_c: A paper clip has no cells when observed under a microscope
questions.choice_d: A paper clip can be picked up easily

questions.stem: In an investigation, why should students observe more than one area of a sample on the slide?
questions.choice_a: Cells are always in the center of the slide
questions.choice_b: Cells may be unevenly distributed, so multiple views give stronger evidence
questions.choice_c: Observing more areas makes the microscope brighter
questions.choice_d: Only multicellular organisms require multiple observations

questions.stem: A student observes a single-celled organism in pond water. Which explanation best describes how this organism can be alive with only one cell?
questions.choice_a: It is not alive until it becomes multicellular
questions.choice_b: One cell can perform all functions needed for life within that organism
questions.choice_c: It is alive only because pond water is alive
questions.choice_d: It is alive only if it moves fast enough to see

questions.stem: Which claim is best supported by the evidence "Cells were observed in the sample"?
questions.choice_a: The sample is living or came from something living
questions.choice_b: The sample is definitely an animal
questions.choice_c: The sample is nonliving because cells are too small
questions.choice_d: The sample is made of only one organ
